characters.name: Rizzoli
characters.description: Action Girl: Would you really expect anything less from a cop? Jane rarely, if ever, shies away from danger and she's willing to pursue a perp even when injured. Adaptational Attractiveness: In the books that the series is based on, Jane Rizzoli is consistently described as plain or average looking. This is a significant characteristic, as she tends to have an irrational jealousy and dislike of beautiful women. She's also described at petite in stature, but here, she's being played by the tall and gorgeous Angie Harmon (though Harmon has played Jane as a little more rough and tumble as time went on). Adaptational Nice Guy: Jane was not the nicest person in the books, being brisque and abrasive to pretty much everyone. Here, she's aJerk with a Heart of Goldon herworstdays and is a pleasant, if still snarky, woman otherwise. Aloof Dark-Haired Girl: Rizzoli is a tall, mature, dark-haired woman but the aloofness is downplayed, since she's snarky but not entirely unapproachable. Ascended Extra: Rizzoli is actually a secondary character in "The Surgeon", the first book in the series, and author Gerritsen had planned to kill her off before positive reader feedback changed her mind.

characters.name: Isles
characters.description: Abnormal Allergy: Fibbing and making guesses with no science or evidence to back it up will break her out into a rash. No, really! And Jane absolutely loves to exploit this for her amusement. Adaptational Attractiveness: It's not as extreme a case as with Jane. Maura is described as "attractive" in the books, but as played by Sasha Alexander she is far more stunning than one would have imagined. Adaptation Dye-Job: Maura is anEerie Pale-Skinned Brunettethe books. All Women Love Shoes:Especiallytelling is her reaction when Jane quips that she hid her shoes. Oh, and she provides the page image. Ambiguously Bi: Maura is clearly interested in men and has a number of boyfriends in the series. But, even discounting the ton ofHomoerotic Subtextshe has with Jane, she's put an awful lot of thought into what kind of women she'd be into if she were a lesbian, and she makes some comments that indicate that she wouldn't mind having sex with a woman.

characters.name: Frankie Rizzoli
characters.description: Annoying Younger Sibling: While he's not "annoying" per say, he does tend to get on Jane's nerves. Embarrassing First Name: Turns out "Frankie" is short forFrancesco. He is not particularly amused about anyone finding out. Passed-Over Promotion: In the early seasons, he works on making detective and shadows both Korsak and Frost. He comes close to making detective in Season 3, but he's skipped over in favor ofRiley Cooperfrom the drug unit. In the Season 4 premiere, he finally makes detective in the drug unit, though he later drifts from department to department before ending up in Homicide.

characters.name: Vincent Korsak
characters.description: Abhorrent Admirer: To Jane in the books. He eventually gets over it and falls for her mother. Adaptational Attractiveness: Hardly a male model in his TV incarnation, but still much better looking than he's described in the books. Adaptation Relationship Overhaul: In the books, he has a creepy fondness for Jane before entering a relationship with her mother. In the TV show, he's explicitly Jane's mentor and a friend of Angela's. Da Chief: After being promoted to Sergeant, Korsak is put in charge of a small team of detectives: himself, Rizzoli and Frost. Friend to All Living Things: Korsak is constantly rescuing animals. Jane and Frost often call him "Dr. Doolittle" every so often.

characters.name: Barry Frost
characters.description: Adapted Out: In the TV series, Frost is unmarried. Afraid of Blood: Especially in the first season, Frost's squeamishness and physical discomfort at the sight of blood and dead bodies makes him the butt of many jibes from his more hardened colleagues. He slowly gets better once he starts helping Frankie in becoming Detective. Beware the Nice Ones:In the bookKeepsake, after Jane makes a snide comment about his attraction to a beautiful witness, he turns on her and snaps,"Fuck you, Rizzoli."and proceeds to chew her out about her persistentIrrational Hatredof beautiful women. Jane notes that Frost is usually such an easygoingNice Guythat to see him react like this is downright scary.In the TV series, Frost is one of the nicest people you'll ever meet, but when he gets angry,he gets angry. This is shown as early in the pilot episode where Hoyt asks Jane if she dreams about him and if he's her lover, causing Frost to leap out of his seat and scream, "That's enough, you son of a bitch! That's enough!" Jane notes that Frost is usually such an easygoingNice Guythat to see him react like this is downright scary. That's enough!"

characters.name: Lt. Sean Cavanaugh
characters.description: Cruel Mercy:He corners Paddy in the men's restroom in the courthouse with the intent to kill him. When he learns from Maura that Paddy's ex-lover Hope is testifying against him, Cavanaugh decides to spare him if only because Hope's "betrayal" is better than simply killing him. Da Chief: He's in charge of the homicide unit and therefore Jane, Frost, and Korsak's boss. It's Personal: In Season 4, he develops an intense hate for Paddy Doyleafter discovering he murdered his wife and child. Screw the Rules, I'm Doing What's Right!: Cavanaugh might be a cop, but he's willing to bend the rules if the need arises. In Season 2, he holds off on calling the commissioner to stop a race so Rizzoli can catch the shooter.

characters.name: Nina Holiday
characters.description: Black and Nerdy: Primarily serves as the team's tech expertafter Frost's death.

characters.name: Dr. Pike
characters.description: Super OCD: One of the reasons why none of Homicide like him, least of all Maura. Tsundere: During his drunken rant, he reveals he'sactually attracted to Maura and her intelligence, but he's too afraid to actually confess. Maura is actually quite off-put by this, but it's clear she doesn'treciprocateas she still finds his attitude to be lacking. Unknown Rival: He considers himself Maura's superior. She barely gives him the time of day and thinks he's an annoyance. Hilariously,he reveals in a drunken rant he actuallylikesher. Upper-Class Twit: While it's murky if he comes from a high-class background like Maura, he has the education to back it up. Unfortunately, he really lives up to the "twit" part by being obnoxious and condescending to everyone, even the police he's supposed to be helping.

characters.name: Angela Rizzoli
characters.description: Amazingly Embarrassing Parents: Even though Jane is in her thirties, she still often finds her mother's behaviour embarrassing. Dark Secret: She was going around taking up any odd job she could find and acting funny any time money was mentioned.Her husband cheated on their taxes and left her holding a $27,000 debt.She doesn't want to let Jane and Frankie know so she can keep him looking good for them, but they find it out. My Beloved Smother: She is very protective of her grown-up children, who often are more than a little embarrassed or irritated at what they perceive as her attempts to control their lives. Parental Favoritism: Jane is blatantly ignored in favor of her brothers, especially Frankie. She still loves Jane in her own little way. Parental Substitute: To Maura. This is despite the fact Maura isHappily Adoptedand has a good relationship with her mother, though this can be chalked up to Constance and her husband being away far too often to actually have a presence in Maura's life.

characters.name: Tommy Rizzoli
characters.description: Fatal Flaw: His temper. It's gotten him into one too many altercations in the past and caused him to pick fights that only serve to screw him over. Foolish Sibling, Responsible Sibling: He's the Foolish to Jane and Frankie's Responsible. His story arc revolves around him getting his life together, especially after he has his son T.J. The Ghost: For Season 1 as he's in prison. He shows up as a recurring character in Season 2 and afterward. Hidden Depths:Despite his tendency to get in trouble, he's a skilled chess player. He spends a whole episode dueling with Maura. The same episode reveals Jane taught him.Season 4 reveals Tommy isa recovering alcoholic. Up until he learned about his dad's cancer, he'd been sober. Despite his tendency to get in trouble, he's a skilled chess player. He spends a whole episode dueling with Maura. The same episode reveals Jane taught him.

characters.name: Paddy Doyle
characters.description: At Least I Admit It: While he does justify his actions by hurting only those who deserve it, he doesn't sugarcoat or downplay what he does. He's a scumbag and he knows it. Cruel Mercy:InS4E4, Cavanaugh learns Paddy killed his wife and child in an attempt to get rid of him. Upon learning this, he's furious and attempts to kill Paddy in the men's bathroom at the courthouse. When Maura tells Paddy Hope is testifying against him, Cavanaugh spares him because he thinks Paddy living with the knowledge that the love of his life betrayed him is a better fate. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: There are only two things that matter to him: his daughter Maura and his former lover Hope. They are literally the only two things he will go to hell and back for.Yet despite this, his love for them is not enough to declare himself guilty to get the feds off their backs. Evil Parents Want Good Kids: He says his son Colin was "too much" like him, implying he wished his son had put his computer skills to better use. He's happy Maura is doing good work as a police mortician. Hypocrite: He states he never hurt women or children.Season 4 reveals there was at least one exception: Cavanaugh's wife and infant son.

characters.name: Patrick Doyle Sr.
characters.description: Abusive Parents: He told Paddy that if he didn't stop seeing Hope, he'd kill them both. Paddy thinks he would even try and kill Maura if he learned her existence, hence why he told Hope their daughter died and gave Maura to Constance Isles.

characters.name: Dr. Hope Martin
characters.description: Adaptational Heroism: She's aSerial Killerin the books. My Greatest Failure: Once described getting pregnant with Maura as her greatest mistake (when she thought the baby had died at birth). Poor Communication Kills: She says her greatest mistake was being with Maura, something she herself takes very hard. What Hopereallymeant was how heartbroken she'd been when she thought Maura died at birth.

characters.name: Charles Hoyt
characters.description: Abhorrent Admirer: He clearly lusts after Jane, even asking her if she ever dreams about him and thinks of him as her lover when they meet in prison. Jane doesnotappreciate his obsession. Arch-Enemy: A personal enemy of Jane's. Even in death, he still finds ways to haunt her. Calling Card: While the teacup is a signature technique of Hoyt's, he incapacitated his victims using a stun gun. Jane states they withheld this detail from the media, so the fact they find it on a new pair of victims while he's in prison informs them he's trained an apprentice. The Corrupter: His second apprentice was an abused housewife. Once he sunk his claws into her after killing her husband, he taught her everything he knew.He technically trained a fourth and a fifth by proxy, though they were already fucked up people to begin with. Fatal Flaw: His obsession with Jane ultimately proves to be his undoing. In his first rematch with Jane after their first run-in, he draws out the scare tactics instead of trying to kill her outright. His secondand finalattempt fairs no better as he creates an elaborate scheme tokill her before cancer claims him. Had he just killed Jane right when he had heralong with Maura, he would have won.
